_what: The post-migrate assertion pass re-runs every `do $$` block of every migration against the database the WHOLE set built, in lexical order, each in its own transaction that is rolled back. A block written when its batch was applied can be made false by a LATER batch that legitimately changes what it asserted; such a block is listed here, beside the later file(s) that changed it and a final-state replacement that restates EVERY assertion of the block as it stands at the end of the set. The replacement runs in the block's place.
_guards: Three, enforced by scripts/db/run.mjs on every `make db-migrate-clean`: (1) a block NOT listed here must pass as written; (2) a block listed here must still FAIL as written, with SQLSTATE P0001 (its own raise, not a syntax error), or the entry is stale and the pass fails; (3) the replacement must pass. A migration that makes an earlier block false therefore fails migrate-clean until the same change adds an entry here -- changing another batch's guarantee is a reviewable line in the diff, never a side effect.
_editing: Migrations are never edited (migration invariant 1). Replacements are not migrations and are edited when a later batch supersedes them again. Each `SUPERSEDED BY` comment inside a replacement names the later file that made that change necessary; everything else in the replacement is the original block word for word.
